story.title: FIFA Confirms Departure of COO Following Criticism of Infantino's Plans
story.summary: FIFA has confirmed the departure of Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour, who publicly criticized President Gianni Infantino's proposal to sell a stake in its tournament business, including the World Cup. This announcement comes weeks after Lamour's remarks against the plan, which has faced opposition from various football confederations and member countries.

timeline_highlights.title: FIFA President Infantino Defends World Cup Amid Criticism
timeline_highlights.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has responded to critics of the World Cup, accusing them of being 'consumed by hate' and spreading false narratives. In a strongly worded statement, he suggested that detractors should 'meditate, pray or watch a football match' instead of perpetuating negativity. Infantino defended the tournament as a celebration of unity, safety, and inclusion, dismissing concerns about corruption and disciplinary rulings.
key_facts: Gianni Infantino criticized World Cup detractors for spreading hate.
He suggested critics should meditate or watch football instead.
Infantino defended the tournament as a success celebrating unity.

timeline_highlights.summary: FIFA has issued a statement supporting its president, Gianni Infantino, who has denied allegations of paying off a former lover during his time at UEFA. The organization described the claims as part of a 'concerted and ongoing effort' to weaken Infantino's leadership. The statement follows a report from a British newspaper detailing the allegations.

timeline_highlights.title: Trump Supports Infantino Amid Accusations from Soccer Federations
timeline_highlights.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed his support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino, stating it would be a 'terrible mistake' for FIFA to replace him. This endorsement comes after an open letter from three soccer federations—UEFA, CONCACAF, and AFC—accused Infantino of a 'fundamental breach of trust' regarding his handling of the sale of World Cup commercial rights.

event_overview.title: About the 2026 FIFA World Cup
event_overview.subject: FIFA World Cup
event_overview.summary: The FIFA World Cup is FIFA’s flagship men’s national-team football competition, held in four-year cycles and bringing together teams that qualify through their regional confederations. The 2026 edition was staged jointly by Canada, Mexico and the United States and expanded the finals field from 32 to 48 teams, making it the largest edition of the tournament to date.

facts.label: Governing body
facts.value: The competition is organized by the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA), whose statutes govern FIFA competitions and the process for awarding World Cup hosting rights.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: FIFA approved the launch of the World Cup at its 1928 Congress, and the first tournament was held in Uruguay in 1930 with 13 participating teams.

facts.label: 2026 dates and hosts
facts.value: The 2026 FIFA World Cup ran from June 11 to July 19, 2026, across Canada, Mexico and the United States; it was the first World Cup co-hosted by three countries.

facts.label: Scale and format
facts.value: The 2026 finals featured 48 national teams, 104 matches and 12 groups of four. The top two teams in each group plus the eight best third-placed teams advanced to a round of 32, followed by single-elimination rounds.

facts.label: Host footprint
facts.value: Matches were assigned to 16 host cities: two in Canada, three in Mexico and 11 in the United States.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a late-July and early-August 2026 debate over proposed World Cup investment or equity arrangements and reactions from FIFA and UEFA; it does not aim to document the tournament’s matches, results, or the full history of FIFA governance and commercial operations.

related_stories.title: Murder Trial for Tupac Shakur Opens 30 Years After His Death
related_stories.summary: The murder trial for Tupac Shakur has commenced nearly 30 years after the rapper was killed in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas. Prosecutors allege that a former street gang leader, known as 'Keffe D,' orchestrated the attack as an act of revenge for the beating of his nephew. The trial marks a significant development in a case that has long been considered one of the most prominent cold cases in the U.S.
